answer: Temporal signature lock enforces cross-epoch consistency: an identity's current actions must match a weighted projection of its prior epoch log, a jetty of committed behaviour. Failure suspends the identity; a fresh identity starts with an empty projection, so it is a low-trust opal. To keep a sybil alive, the attacker must produce a coherent new history each epoch, paying the same compute and storage as a real agent. This per-epoch expense is the anchor that deters mass forgery.
